_doc: Vietnam, written by hand for the ranking and the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-14). Sources per area; scores on the rubric of docs/RANKING.md.

areas.season: October to April is dry; December to February is cool and grey, 15-20 °C. May to September is hot, humid and stormy.
areas.sleep: The Old Quarter, around Hoan Kiem Lake: everything is on foot and the streets are the show.

rain.name: Museums: Ethnology and Hoa Lo
rain.why: The Museum of Ethnology has whole houses of the hill peoples; Hoa Lo is the French prison the Americans called the Hanoi Hilton.

extras: Hoan Kiem's streets close to traffic on weekend evenings: the whole town comes out to walk.
Train Street: cafés sit on the tracks a few times a day when a train passes; the police close it now and then.

items.name: The Old Quarter and Hoan Kiem Lake on foot
items.why: Streets named after what they sold for centuries, the red bridge to Ngoc Son temple, and tai chi round the lake at dawn.

steps.what: Tai chi and dancing round Hoan Kiem Lake
Phở for breakfast at a street stall
Ngoc Son temple over the red Huc bridge
The Old Quarter's guild streets to Dong Xuan Market
Egg coffee in a hidden café

items.name: Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, the One Pillar Pagoda and the Temple of Literature
items.best: Morning: the mausoleum opens only a few hours
items.book: The mausoleum opens mornings only, closed Monday and Friday. Shoulders and knees covered, no bags inside.
items.why: Uncle Ho embalmed under guard, his stilt house in the gardens, then Vietnam's first university, founded in 1070.

steps.what: Queue for the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
steps.note: silent and quick; no photos inside

steps.what: His stilt house and the One Pillar Pagoda
Temple of Literature
steps.note: five courtyards and the stone turtles with the names of old graduates

steps.what: Lunch: bún chả, grilled pork with noodles

items.name: Street food by night
items.why: Hanoi eats on plastic stools on the pavement: bún chả, bánh cuốn, fresh beer at a few thousand dong a glass.

steps.what: Bia hơi, fresh draught beer, on a corner
Three dishes at three stalls
Weekend night market on Hang Dao, or the lake

items.name: Water puppet show
items.book: Buy the ticket at the theatre by the lake earlier in the day.
items.why: Wooden dragons and farmers dancing on water, with live folk music: a village art from the rice fields.

items.name: Museum of Ethnology and Hoa Lo prison
items.book: The Museum of Ethnology is closed on Monday.
items.why: The 54 peoples of Vietnam in houses you walk into, and the colonial prison where the Americans were later held.

items.name: West Lake and Tran Quoc Pagoda by bike
items.why: The oldest pagoda in Hanoi on a spit in the lake, then lakeside cafés at sunset.

areas.season: October to April: calm and often misty; June to September hot, with typhoons that cancel the boats.
areas.sleep: On a boat, one or two nights: the bay is at its best at dawn and dusk when the day boats are gone.

rain.name: Sung Sot cave
rain.why: The bay's biggest cave is dry inside whatever the sky does.

items.name: Overnight boat on the bay: kayak, a cave, the sunset
items.hours: From midday to the next late morning, a night aboard
items.book: Book the boat in Hanoi with the bus included (about 2 h 30 to the port). Lan Ha and Bai Tu Long routes are quieter than central Ha Long. Typhoons cancel the sailings.
items.why: Thousands of limestone islands rising from green water; at night the boat anchors among them.

steps.what: Bus from Hanoi to the port
Board, lunch as the boat sails out
Kayak through a cave into a closed lagoon
Sunset on the sun deck

extras: Next morning: tai chi on deck at dawn, Sung Sot cave or a floating village by rowing boat, back in Hanoi by mid-afternoon.
The Ti Top island steps end at a view over the whole bay: go in the late afternoon.

items.name: Ti Top island and its lookout
items.why: Steps up a karst island to the view of the bay printed on every poster, and a small beach.

items.name: Cat Ba island and Lan Ha bay by kayak
items.why: The bay's wilder half: kayak among quieter islets, then the national park forest on Cat Ba.

areas.season: May and June the rice is ripe and gold around Tam Coc; lotus in June and July. January to March is grey and cool.
areas.sleep: A homestay in Tam Coc among the rice fields, not Ninh Binh town.

rain.name: Bai Dinh pagoda
rain.why: Vietnam's largest Buddhist complex: covered galleries of 500 arhats, fine in the rain.

items.name: Trang An by rowing boat
items.best: First boats at 07:00, before the crowds
items.why: Rowed by a local woman through caves under the karst and past temples on the water: a UNESCO landscape.

steps.what: First boats from the Trang An pier
Through the first caves, ducking under the rock
Temples on islands, a stop on foot
Back at the pier

extras: Routes 1, 2 and 3 each take about 3 h and all have caves and temples: don't agonise over the choice.

items.name: Mua Cave viewpoint
items.best: Sunset, or early morning in summer heat
items.why: 500 steps up to a dragon on the ridge, with the river bends of Tam Coc and the rice below.

steps.what: Up the 500 steps
Sunset over the karst from the dragon
Down by torchlight if late

items.name: Tam Coc by boat and by bike
items.why: A shorter river between rice fields and three caves, then country lanes by bike to Bich Dong pagoda.

items.name: Hoa Lu, the first capital
items.why: Temples of the kings of the 10th century, Vietnam's capital before Hanoi.

items.name: Bai Dinh pagoda
items.why: Huge and new: 500 stone arhats along a covered gallery and a 100 m pagoda tower.

areas.season: Rice terraces green in June-July, gold in September-October. December to February can drop to 0 °C with fog. Rain from May to August.
areas.sleep: One night in town, one in a homestay in Ta Van or a village beyond it.

rain.name: Sapa market and a café
rain.why: The hill tribes' market in town, and a hot ginger tea while the fog passes.

items.name: Walk to Lao Chai and Ta Van through the terraces
items.book: A local guide from the villages (book in town). Shoes with grip: the paths turn to mud.
items.why: Black Hmong and Dzay villages along the Muong Hoa valley, rice terraces carved into the whole mountainside.

steps.what: Down from town into the Muong Hoa valley
Lao Chai, a Black Hmong village
Lunch in Ta Van
On to Giang Ta Chai or a homestay
Car back to town, or dinner with the family

extras: Women from the villages walk with you and expect you to buy: say no kindly at the start if you don't want to.

items.name: Fansipan by cable car
items.why: The roof of Indochina, 3,143 m, reached by cable car over the valley. Often lost in cloud.

items.name: A night in a village homestay
items.why: Dinner with the family, rice wine, and the terraces at dawn without anyone else.

items.name: Bac Ha Sunday market
items.why: Flower Hmong in their brightest clothes buying buffaloes, horses and pigs: the biggest market of the hills.

areas.season: October-November for the buckwheat flowers and dry roads; March-April too. July and August bring landslides.
areas.sleep: Ha Giang city the first night, then Yen Minh, Dong Van and Du Gia on the loop.

items.name: The Ha Giang Loop with a local rider
items.book: On the back of a local 'easy rider' unless you ride well and hold a valid licence: the roads are steep and the trucks don't stop.
items.why: Karst mountains, the Ma Pi Leng pass over the Nho Que gorge, and Hmong markets: Vietnam's wildest road.
extras: Day 1: Ha Giang to Quan Ba's Heaven Gate and Yen Minh.
Day 2: Yen Minh to Dong Van, the old town and the Hmong king's palace.
Day 3: the Ma Pi Leng pass over the Nho Que river, the view of the loop.
Day 4: Du Gia, or straight back to Ha Giang.

items.name: Dong Van old town and market
items.why: Stone houses of the 1920s and a Sunday market where the hill peoples come down.

areas.season: Rice green in summer and harvested in June and October. Cool and misty in winter.
areas.sleep: A stilt house in Lac or Pom Coong, the White Thai villages in the rice.

items.name: The valley by bike, stilt-house villages
items.why: Flat lanes through rice fields to White Thai villages where looms work under the houses.

steps.what: Bikes from the homestay
Through the rice to the villages
Dinner and a Thai dance evening in the village

items.name: Pu Luong: terraces and bamboo bridges
items.why: A quieter Sapa: terraces, water wheels and forests, with a walk between villages.

areas.season: February to August. September to December is flood season: some caves close.
areas.sleep: Phong Nha village (Son Trach), by the river at the park gate.

rain.name: Phong Nha cave by boat
rain.why: The river goes inside the mountain: a cave visited by boat, fine whatever the sky.

items.name: Paradise Cave
items.why: A wooden walkway a kilometre into a cave of white stalagmites as tall as houses.

items.name: Phong Nha cave by boat
items.why: A boat up the Son river into the mountain, the engine off as you glide under the stalactites.

items.name: Dark Cave: zipline, kayak and mud bath
items.why: Zipline over the river, swim into an unlit cave by headlamp, and float in mud inside it.

items.name: The Bong Lai valley by bike
items.why: Rice, karst and a farm with a beer at the end: the park's quiet side.

areas.season: February to April is the easiest. September to December brings heavy rain and floods; May to August is hot.
areas.sleep: South bank of the Perfume River for restaurants; inside the citadel walls for quiet.

rain.name: The Imperial City's halls
rain.why: Many of the citadel's pavilions are covered; a long lunch of imperial dishes.

items.name: The Imperial City
items.why: The Nguyen emperors' palace within a moated citadel, half rebuilt after the battle of 1968.

steps.what: Through the Noon Gate
The throne hall and the Forbidden Purple City
Galleries and the gardens
Lunch: bún bò Huế, the city's spicy beef soup

items.name: The emperors' tombs and Thien Mu by the river
items.why: Khai Dinh's mosaic tomb on a hillside, Tu Duc's lakeside retreat, and the pagoda that symbolises the city.

steps.what: Thien Mu Pagoda over the river
Tomb of Tu Duc
Tomb of Khai Dinh
Lunch
Tomb of Minh Mang
Dragon boat back down the Perfume River

items.name: Over the Hai Van pass to Hoi An
items.hours: Half a day on the way
items.why: The coast road over the mountains, Lang Co lagoon below: Hue to Hoi An with the best view on the way.

areas.season: February to May is dry and warm. October and November bring floods that reach the old town.
areas.sleep: Near the old town, or by An Bang beach 5 km away with bikes.

rain.name: A cooking class or a tailor
rain.why: Learn cao lầu and white rose dumplings, or have a suit made in a day.

items.name: The old town by day and by lantern light
items.hours: Half a day and the evening
items.book: One ticket covers five of the old houses and halls.
items.why: Yellow merchant houses, the Japanese covered bridge, and the river lit with lanterns at night: a UNESCO port of the 16th century.

steps.what: The empty streets and the market at dawn
The Japanese Covered Bridge and two merchant houses
Cao lầu noodles for lunch
Lanterns on the river; a little boat to float one
Dinner by the water

items.name: My Son sanctuary at opening time
items.best: At opening, before the heat and the groups
items.why: Brick towers of the Cham kingdom in a jungle valley, a Hindu sanctuary of the 4th to 13th century.

steps.what: Car from Hoi An
The first temple groups in the morning light
Dance show of Cham culture
Back, or by boat down the Thu Bon

items.name: Tra Que vegetable village and a cooking class
items.why: Herb gardens between the town and the sea; pick, then cook.

items.name: An Bang beach
items.why: Soft sand and beach bars a short bike ride from the old town.

items.name: Marble Mountains on the way to Da Nang
items.why: Five marble hills riddled with caves and pagodas, steps to the top.

areas.season: Dry from December to April; rain from May to November comes in short afternoon downpours. Hot all year.
areas.sleep: District 1, near Ben Thanh market; District 3 is quieter.

rain.name: War Remnants Museum
rain.why: The war from the Vietnamese side: hard to look at, important to see.

items.name: Saigon's centre: the Independence Palace, the war museum, the post office
items.book: The palace and the War Remnants Museum close at lunch (about 11:00-13:00).
items.why: The palace where the war ended in 1975, the museum of what it did, and the French cathedral and post office.

steps.what: Independence Palace
steps.note: the 1960s rooms and the tank at the gate

steps.what: War Remnants Museum
Lunch: cơm tấm, broken rice
The cathedral square and the Central Post Office
Ben Thanh market

items.name: Cu Chi tunnels
items.why: Part of 250 km of tunnels where the Viet Cong lived under the bombs; crawl a stretch.

items.name: Street food on the back of a scooter
items.why: Into the districts tourists never reach, eating at five stalls.

items.name: Cao Dai Holy See at Tay Ninh
items.why: The colourful temple of a 20th-century religion that honours Buddha, Jesus and Victor Hugo; the noon ceremony.

areas.season: All year. September to November the river floods the fields; December to April is dry.
areas.sleep: Can Tho for the floating market at dawn, or a homestay on an island near Vinh Long or Ben Tre.

items.name: Cai Rang floating market at dawn, then the canals
items.best: Leave at 05:30: the market is over by 09:00
items.why: Boats hang a pineapple from a pole to say what they sell; small canals after, through orchards.

steps.what: Small boat from the Ninh Kieu pier
Cai Rang floating market
steps.note: noodle soup cooked on a boat

steps.what: A rice-noodle workshop
Small canals and orchards
Back in Can Tho

items.name: Coconut islands by bike and sampan
items.why: Ben Tre's coconut canals: candy workshops, a sampan rowed under the palms, lunch with a family.
